//: Shared visualization corpus — the anti-drift contract between the Rust validator (build_viz_payload, src-tauri/src/chat/tools/viz.rs) and the frontend rendering gate (parseVizPayload, src/lib/viz.ts). Both MUST accept every marker in `accept` and reject every marker in `reject`. The bugs this pins: (1) the tool and the marker emitter disagreed on a JSON-STRINGIFIED payload, so every card rendered while its step row read 'Preparing visualization'; (2) the gate rejected the normalizer's own outputs (table align:'left', timeline detail:'') and showed 'Visualization unavailable' for cards the backend had accepted. A new viz kind adds rows here from BOTH languages' tests, rather than either side growing a second hand-written opinion.

reject.why: an align that is neither left nor right
a task-board task with no title
a timeline event with no label
a stack section that is not a (viz, payload) pair
a stack section with an invalid child (precise path: sections[0])
a color that could smuggle CSS
